clue.text: Cabinet's private information given publicity endlessly

definitions.note: the definition is the cabinet; the 's stands for 'is', linking it to the wordplay

parts.note: private information is a secret

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter of the synonym is dropped

parts.note: a matter given publicity has been aired

explanation.surface: A government Cabinet's confidential matters keep leaking to the press.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests government ministers, but it is a piece of furniture. 'endlessly' cuts the D from AIRED to leave AIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretaire is a writing desk with drawers and a closing front, a type of cabinet.

clue.text: Son unwell — one lies horizontally

parts.note: unwell means ill

explanation.surface: A sick son is lying down flat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bedridden son; the definition describes a ledge that lies flat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sill is a horizontal ledge of a window or door, a piece that lies flat.

clue.text: Mistress of violent nature so cold initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the word is used
violent suggests wild disturbance, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A lover with a violent temperament who is also cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'violent' rearranges NATURESO into OURTESAN, after C from 'cold initially'.
explanation.definitionFit: A courtesan is a kept mistress, especially of a wealthy or noble man.

clue.text: Distinctive spirit of English Society, although briefly hidden

indicators.note: hidden means concealed inside, so the short word goes within the two letters
briefly means shortened, so the word loses its ending to give the informal short spelling

parts.note: although means though

explanation.surface: The spirit of English high society is somewhat concealed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'although briefly' looks like a qualifier on the surface, but it gives the informal short spelling once 'briefly' cuts the word; 'hidden' tucks that inside the two abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethos is the characteristic spirit or guiding beliefs of a community or culture.

clue.text: A couple of females, competent and friendly

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for female, so two of them make FF
competent means able

explanation.surface: Two women who are capable and pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable means good-natured and easy to talk to, warmly sociable.

clue.text: Repudiates diatribes about London's business quarter

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: a diatribe is an angry tirade, a rant
EC is the postcode of the City of London, its financial district

explanation.surface: Someone rejects angry tirades about the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To recant is to retract or renounce a previously held statement or belief.

clue.text: Packing material one used for dry bed

parts.note: a wad is a lump of soft material used for packing or padding
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: Someone stuffs packing material into a makeshift bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A wadi is a riverbed in desert country that is dry except in the rainy season.

clue.text: Lady taking a long time to capture knight

indicators.note: capture means hold within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: ages means a long time
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A lady takes ages to catch a knight in shining armour.
explanation.walkthrough: N for knight comes from chess notation, where K is already the king.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnes is a woman's name, and crosswords often define a name as a lady.

clue.text: Sounds like I am fond of pets in this part of the capital

indicators.note: says the phrase is heard rather than written, matching another phrase spoken aloud

parts.note: a pet lover might say 'I love dogs'

explanation.surface: A dog lover declares affection for pets in part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Dogs is a district of east London, in the Docklands; 'I love dogs' said aloud approximates its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Isle of Dogs is a district of London, the capital, on a bend of the Thames.

clue.text: Well ought to supply this water in Ireland

indicators.note: the two words together supply the answer's letters, sitting across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A well should provide this water in Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: A lough is the Irish word for a lake or sea inlet, a body of water in Ireland.

clue.text: Fan, a clot I suspect that's liable to be disruptive

indicators.note: suspect here means dubious or unreliable, so the letters are not to be trusted in their order and are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone suspects that an idiotic fan is a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I suspect' reads as the speaker's opinion, but 'I' is part of the fodder and 'suspect' alone signals the anagram of FANACLOTI.
explanation.definitionFit: Factional describes splinter groups within a body, which tend to cause division and disruption.

clue.text: Mischief-maker with affectedness improves? Quite the opposite

definitions.note: the definition is the opposite of making better, so it means damages or weakens

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little creature
putting on airs is affected behaviour

explanation.surface: A prankster with pretentious manners seems to be getting better.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the reverse of 'improves', as 'Quite the opposite' says.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to weaken or damage, the opposite of making something better.

clue.text: International agreement that sees top cricketer suspended for a while?

definitions.meaning: a treaty between nations banning nuclear weapons trials

definitions.text: top cricketer suspended for a while?
definitions.meaning: a leading cricketer banned from playing in Test matches would face this, read literally

explanation.surface: A treaty between nations seems to involve a star cricketer being suspended.
explanation.walkthrough: Test matches are international cricket fixtures; a top player barred from them is under a 'Test ban'.
explanation.definitionFit: A test ban treaty is an international agreement forbidding nuclear weapons tests.

clue.text: Sauce can give headache when served with duck

parts.note: a headache in the sense of a nuisance, a pest
a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: Eating duck with a certain sauce gives someone a headache.
explanation.definitionFit: Pesto is an Italian sauce of basil, pine nuts, garlic and cheese.

clue.text: Rare song is surprisingly offered by those putting on an event

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests an unexpected outcome, so the letters come out in a new order

explanation.surface: A rarely heard song is offered by the people staging a concert.
explanation.definitionFit: Organisers are the people who arrange and run an event.

clue.text: Determination to crack again

definitions.meaning: to crack a puzzle is to solve it

explanation.surface: Someone shows the willpower to break a code a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Resolve means firm determination; split as RE-SOLVE it means solve once more.

clue.text: Stuff for someone very young you put in milky drink

indicators.note: put in means inserted, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a latte is coffee made with a lot of hot milk
ye is an old word for you

explanation.surface: Something for a baby, with a milky drink you add.
explanation.definitionFit: A layette is a set of clothes, bedding and other items for a newborn baby.

clue.text: Pompous, like one able to look down from a great height?

definitions.text: like one able to look down from a great height?
definitions.meaning: someone walking on stilts, raised far above others

explanation.surface: A pompous person seems to look down on others from on high.
explanation.definitionFit: Stilted means stiffly formal and pompous; literally it can mean raised up on stilts.

clue.text: Idiot getting a hangover?

definitions.meaning: after drinking too much one wakes with a heavy, dull feeling in the head

explanation.surface: A fool gets a hangover.
explanation.definitionFit: A thickhead is a stupid person; read as two words, a thick head describes a hangover.

clue.text: Cross girl you had once found harbouring love

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
love is nil in tennis, the letter O
ye'd is an old form of 'you had'

explanation.surface: An angry girl, as she used to be, is discovered sheltering a lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' is an adjective, angry. 'once' marks the archaic YE'D for 'you had'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross and annoyed are both everyday synonyms for irritated or angry.

clue.text: Dying to find relaxation at end of final month

indicators.note: at end of places one piece after the other

parts.note: DEC is the abbreviation for December, the last month
ease means relaxation

explanation.surface: Someone relaxes at the end of December, as the year dies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dying' is a noun here, the act of death.
explanation.definitionFit: Decease is a formal word for death, the act of dying.

clue.text: 'Elvis' sits by vehicle making music for those passing by

definitions.text: making music for those passing by

indicators.note: sits by means is placed next to, so one piece follows the other

parts.note: a bus is a vehicle
Elvis Presley was known as the King of rock and roll

explanation.surface: An Elvis impersonator sits beside a bus, performing for passers-by.
explanation.definitionFit: Busking is performing music in public places for money from passers-by.

clue.text: Something hairy makes one react angrily

definitions.meaning: a short stiff hair, as on a brush or a pig
to show irritation or indignation, with hackles raised

explanation.surface: A hairy thing makes someone lose their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: A bristle is a stiff hair; to bristle is to react with anger or indignation.

clue.text: Group beside home in small picture?

indicators.note: beside means next to, placing one piece alongside the other

parts.note: at home is 'in'
a set is a group

explanation.surface: A group photo taken next to the house.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small picture or map set within a larger one; the question mark flags the loose definition.

clue.text: Brain? It's what a rower may need, we hear

indicators.note: says the word is heard spoken, so it stands for a word sounding the same

parts.note: a scull is a type of oar

explanation.surface: Is intelligence what an oarsman needs?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brain?' is a loose definition: the skull is the bony case of the brain, and the question mark admits it.
explanation.definitionFit: The skull is the bony casing of the head that houses the brain.

clue.text: Wind, one penetrating church recess

indicators.note: penetrating means getting into, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a nook is a small recess
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A draught blows into an alcove of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinook is a warm dry wind descending the eastern side of the Rocky Mountains.

clue.text: Start where the actors are being filmed

definitions.meaning: the beginning of something, as of an illness

definitions.text: where the actors are being filmed
definitions.meaning: actors filming are on the film set

explanation.surface: Shooting begins where the cast is being filmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Onset means beginning or start; split in two, on set is where actors work during filming.

clue.text: Elizabeth's heading off to become an artist

indicators.note: heading off means the head, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: Betty is a pet form of Elizabeth; the 's is just the possessive

explanation.surface: Elizabeth leaves to pursue a career as a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: William Etty was a 19th-century English painter known for nudes.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was an English painter, so he is an artist.

clue.text: Sparkling old lover of the upper class with silly banter

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
U is the conventional label for upper class

indicators.note: silly means foolish or messed about, so the word banter is rearranged

explanation.surface: A former aristocratic lover chats foolishly and brightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuberant means full of lively energy and high spirits, effervescent.

clue.text: Exhausted writer sitting in street

indicators.note: sitting in means placed inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A tired author is sitting out in the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' looks like an author, but it is the pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Spent means used up, worn out, with no energy left.

clue.text: What shop may put on in Greater Manchester area

definitions.meaning: a shop puts on a reduction of prices for a period
a town in Greater Manchester, in north-west England

explanation.surface: A shop holds an event somewhere in Greater Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: Shops hold a sale; Sale is also a town in Trafford, Greater Manchester.

clue.text: Yet pleader will go wild again and again

indicators.note: going wild means running out of control, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A pleader in court will lose control yet again.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeatedly means over and over, time after time.
